concepts.def: Long-term shift in global weather patterns and temperatures.
Weather is short-term; climate is the long-term average.
Trapping of heat in the atmosphere by certain gases.
CO₂, methane (CH₄) and nitrous oxide (N₂O) are the main ones.
Last 2.6 million years with repeated glacial-interglacial cycles.
Rise in average global surface temperature over time.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Climate is the long-term average of weather (usually 30+ years).

Climate change means these averages are shifting — temperatures, rainfall and seasons.

It is natural AND human-caused.

Solar energy enters the atmosphere and warms Earth's surface.

Some heat is re-radiated and trapped by greenhouse gases like CO₂, CH₄ and N₂O.

Without it Earth would be ~33°C colder!

Since 1850 global temperatures have risen by about 1.1°C.

The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to limit warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

Beyond this, impacts become severe and irreversible.
